First release of STFIDE, an Arduino-style IDE for the STFKart board (an Arduino Uno / ATmega328P).

## Downloads

- **Windows:** `STFIDE Setup 0.1.0.exe`
- **Linux:** the `.AppImage` (any distro) or the `.deb` (Debian/Ubuntu)

arduino-cli, the AVR toolchain, avrdude and all libraries are bundled, so it works offline.

## What's in it

- Code editor (Monaco) with Arduino autocomplete that knows your pin names, hover help and multi-file sketches.
- **Circuit tab:** place parts next to the STFKart, wire them to its pins, name them, and STFIDE writes the setup code. Ready-made parts include an ultrasonic sensor, DHT11/DHT22, DS18B20, I2C LCD, NeoPixel ring, RGB LED and relay.
- Plain-language warnings for pin clashes, unwired parts and invalid names.
- Verify and Upload with errors marked in the editor and beginner-friendly hints.
- Port picker for Uno-compatible USB chips, and a serial monitor.
- Settings window: English or Türkçe interface, editor font size, sketchbook folder.
- Examples: Blink, Button, Fade, AnalogRead, ServoKnob, InterruptCounter, Melody, WeatherStation, RainbowStrip.

## Known limitations

- **Uploading to a real board has not been tested yet**, and neither has running the installed AppImage. Compiling is tested in CI. Please report any upload problems.
- The installers are not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first launch ("More info" → "Run anyway").
